feedback.overall:
1. Overall assessment  
Strong, credible CV for senior digital leadership roles: the experience shows clear progression, relevant scope, and solid public-sector/platform expertise. It is generally well written and polished, but it feels slightly dense and repetitive, with a few style inconsistencies and limited outcome-focused evidence beyond activity descriptions.

1. Top strengths  
- Clear senior positioning: the headline, summary, and career progression strongly support a digital platform/communications leadership profile.  
- Good credibility: long tenure at NACo, promotion history, and concrete platform scale signals like “10,000+ page website” and “3.5 million annual page views.”  
- Broad, relevant skill mix: combines strategy, governance, analytics, CMS/platform delivery, and multimedia in a way that fits modern digital leadership roles.

1. Top improvements  
- Add more measurable outcomes: several bullets describe responsibilities rather than impact. Include results such as engagement growth, efficiency gains, cost savings, adoption rates, or campaign performance.  
- Reduce duplication: “Core Competencies,” “Topline Skills,” and “Technical + IT” overlap heavily. Consolidating these sections would improve structure and readability.  
- Fix minor style/grammar consistency issues: “social, and multimedia” has an unnecessary comma; punctuation and bullet formatting vary; “French (A2/Learning)” is stylistically awkward—consider “French (A2, improving).” Also standardize title casing (e.g., “Coleman Davis” vs “DAVIS”).
feedback.intro:
Quick assessment: Strong, credible intro with clear seniority and domain focus, but it reads slightly generic and overlaps heavily with the subtitle, core competencies, and NACo experience. It would be stronger with one concrete scale signal and tighter phrasing.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Replace “Senior digital leader” with a more specific positioning line, e.g. “Digital platform and communications systems leader with 12+ years in public-sector and advocacy organizations.”
- Add one proof point from recent experience to increase impact, such as “10,000+ page Drupal migration,” “3.5M annual page views,” or “50+ internal publishers.”
- Tighten the second sentence by grouping related areas: “Leads web modernization, governance, analytics, editorial operations, multimedia, and AI-enabled search/content experiences.”
- Consider revised version: “Digital platform and communications systems leader with 12+ years building enterprise web, governance, and content operations for high-volume public-sector communications. Leads modernization across Drupal platforms, analytics, editorial workflows, multimedia production, and AI-enabled search for complex, mission-driven organizations.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “AI-enabled user experiences” overlaps with core competencies/footer; “AI-enabled search” is more specific and better supported.
- “Platforms, governance models and content operations” closely repeats the subtitle and skills sections.
feedback.coreCompetencies:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant themes, but this block overlaps heavily with the header, Topline Skills, and Technical + IT sections. It would be stronger if tightened to emphasize leadership-level capability areas rather than repeating detailed skill phrases.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Reframe as broader, executive-level competencies: Enterprise web modernization • Digital governance and content operations • Analytics, reporting, and optimization • Cross-channel communications leadership • AI-enabled search and discovery • Workflow automation and systems integration • Public-sector advocacy communications • Multimedia and livestream production
- Standardize style: use “and” instead of mixing “&” with other constructions for a cleaner, more formal tone.
- Consider replacing “editorial systems” with “content operations” to align more directly with the experience section.
- If space is tight, shorten “AI-enabled search and content experiences” to “AI-enabled search and discovery.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Significant overlap with the header summary and all four Topline Skills blocks.
- “Multimedia production and livestream operations” is also repeated in Technical + IT and multiple roles.
feedback.footer:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant examples that reinforce your current positioning, but the block is too dense and repeats themes already covered in Work Experience. Tightening the phrasing and making the format more scannable will improve impact.

Suggested rewrite improvements
- Add a one-line intro such as “Selected recent projects” and format each item as a short, punchy accomplishment rather than a full sentence.
- Tighten wording: “AI-enabled” appears repeatedly; vary language and remove filler like “designed for continued campaign growth.”
- Standardize style and parallel structure, e.g., start each item with a strong verb and keep each to one line.
- Consider this rewrite:  
  AI Hybrid Search — Built a legislative search experience using hybrid retrieval, vector search, structured content workflows, and bill-level chat.  
  We Are Counties Microsite — Developed a Drupal 10 campaign microsite with custom navigation, storytelling modules, and downloadable resources.  
  Organization Anniversary Campaign — Produced a multi-part digital campaign featuring editorial storytelling, archival media, web features, and an interactive conference display.  
  Advocacy Video Series — Launched a recurring advocacy video program across web, email, and social.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- AI search, microsites, and advocacy video work closely overlap with current and NACo experience bullets.
- “Built/Developed” repeats heavily; vary verbs if this section stays.

items.title: Coleman DAVIS
items.subtitle: Digital Platform & Communications Systems Leader
items.content: Senior digital leader with 12+ years of experience building the platforms, governance models and content operations behind high-volume public-sector communications. Leads enterprise web modernization, analytics infrastructure, editorial systems, multimedia production and AI-enabled user experiences for complex, mission-driven organizations.

items.title: Email
items.content: colemandavis4@gmail.com

items.title: Website
items.content: https://colemanpdavis.com/

items.title: Core Competencies
items.content: Enterprise website modernization • Digital governance & editorial systems • Analytics and reporting infrastructure • Multi-channel communications operations • AI-enabled search and content experiences • Workflow automation and platform integration • Advocacy and public-sector communications • Multimedia production and livestream operations

items.title: CV Footer
items.content:
### Recent Projects
**AI Hybrid Search**
Designed an AI-enabled legislative search experience combining hybrid retrieval, structured content workflows, vector search and bill-level AI chat to improve discovery of complex policy content.
**We Are Counties Microsite**
Built a Drupal 10 campaign microsite with custom navigation, interactive storytelling modules, downloadable resources and a modular structure designed for continued campaign growth.
**Organization Anniversary Campaign**
Developed a multi-part digital campaign combining editorial storytelling, archival media, web features and a 10×20-foot interactive conference display connected to the main site.
**Advocacy Video Series**
Built a recurring advocacy video program spanning editorial planning, production and distribution across website, email and social channels.

items.title: Strategic Communications Consultant
items.subtitle: Freelance (full-time engagement)
items.content:
Support a U.S.-based national membership organization on digital strategy, campaign platforms, content operations and enterprise web improvement.
- Build and refine digital systems, workflows and analytics that support coordinated organization-wide communications.
- Develop campaign and storytelling experiences within the organization’s Drupal platform, including custom microsite structures, modular content sections and downloadable member-facing toolkits.
- Deliver CMS development, front-end implementation and technical troubleshooting for large public-facing web properties.
- Advise on governance, usability and operational best practices across web, email, social and multimedia channels.
- Lead development of an AI-enabled search initiative, shaping retrieval strategy, structured content workflows and user-facing discovery design.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, current role with good scope and technical depth, but it reads as a task list. Tighten it around outcomes, scale, and the few contributions that best differentiate this role from your NACo experience.

Suggested edit:
- Open with impact + client context: “Lead digital strategy, platform improvement, and content operations for a U.S. national membership organization, strengthening enterprise communications across web, email, social, and multimedia.”
- Combine overlapping systems/governance bullets: “Built cross-functional workflows, analytics, and governance practices to improve coordination, publishing consistency, and operational efficiency.”
- Make the Drupal/campaign work more outcome-led: “Designed and launched Drupal-based campaign and storytelling experiences, including modular microsites, reusable content components, and downloadable member toolkits.”
- Keep one technical/AI bullet each, with metrics if possible: “Delivered front-end/CMS enhancements and troubleshooting for high-traffic public sites” and “Led an AI-enabled search initiative spanning retrieval design, structured content, and user discovery.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This overlaps with NACo on governance, analytics, and multi-channel operations; avoid repeating generic leadership language.
- Footer projects already cover microsite and AI search—keep this entry focused on role-level impact.

items.title: Director of Digital Media
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led NACo’s digital communications team, overseeing the organization’s website, email, social media and video platforms, along with digital strategy, analytics, governance and budget management.
- Led the redesign and migration of NACo’s 10,000+ page website into a new Drupal platform supporting 3.5 million annual page views, 6,000+ average daily users and 50+ internal publishers.
- Directed NACo’s core digital communications channels, including email newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and social media platforms serving thousands of followers.
- Built NACo’s first broadcast-quality in-house video studio, expanding in-house capacity for advocacy programming, event production and recurring multimedia content.
- Expanded the organization’s analytics infrastructure across GA4, Microsoft Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio and BigQuery, improving reporting and strategic decision-making.
- Strengthened digital operations through clearer governance, publishing standards and cross-department planning systems.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, high-scope leadership entry with good scale metrics. It will be stronger if you tighten the opening, foreground the most strategic outcomes, and avoid repeating channel-management details already covered in earlier NACo roles.

Suggested edit:
- Replace the opening with a sharper scope statement: “Directed NACo’s digital media function, leading web, email, social, video, analytics, governance, and budget management.”
- Reorder bullets to emphasize highest-impact wins first: website migration, analytics infrastructure, in-house studio, then governance/operations.
- Make outcomes more explicit where possible: add % improvements, cost savings, production volume, reporting speed, engagement growth, or reduced vendor reliance.
- Tighten channel bullet to focus on leadership/results, not basic oversight: “Oversaw email and social programs reaching tens of thousands of county officials, aligning distribution with advocacy and member engagement goals.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Directed core digital communications channels” overlaps with the Associate Communications Director entry; keep this one at the strategic/organizational level.
- Video production language overlaps with older NACo roles; emphasize building the studio and expanding institutional capacity, not producing content.

items.title: Associate Communications Director
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led day-to-day digital communications operations across web, email, social media and video, helping scale NACo’s editorial coordination and advocacy communications.
- Managed four recurring weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.
- Produced and expanded a weekly advocacy video update, helping establish video as a recurring policy communications channel.
- Strengthened editorial planning and coordination across communications, advocacy and program teams.
- Helped improve the consistency and effectiveness of NACo’s digital publishing workflows.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression story, but this entry overlaps heavily with the later Director role and earlier Digital Media Manager role. Make it more distinct by emphasizing executional leadership, channel ownership, and any measurable growth or process improvements achieved before promotion.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite the lead to focus on scope and progression: “Directed day-to-day digital communications operations across NACo’s web, email, social and video channels, scaling editorial coordination and advocacy messaging ahead of promotion to Director.”
- Tighten bullets to 3–4 high-value points; combine workflow/editorial bullets into one outcome-focused line.
- Add metrics where possible: newsletter audience size, video cadence/views, publishing volume, turnaround-time reduction, or number of cross-functional teams supported.
- Example structure: “Managed four weekly newsletters reaching [X]+ county officials”; “Produced a weekly advocacy video series, establishing video as a recurring policy channel”; “Built cross-team editorial planning processes that improved publishing consistency and coordination across communications, advocacy and program teams.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “weekly video updates” overlaps with the 2015–2018 role and footer project; keep this version focused on scaling/formalizing the program.
- “publishing workflows/governance” overlaps with the Director role; avoid broad governance language here.

items.title: Digital Strategy & Content Leadership
items.content:
- Enterprise digital strategy
- Editorial systems and governance
- Multi-channel communications leadership
- Public-sector and advocacy messaging
- Audience-focused content planning
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong positioning, but this skills block overlaps heavily with the header, core competencies, and recent roles. It should be tightened to emphasize higher-level leadership themes not already repeated elsewhere.

Suggested edit:
- Replace with sharper, less generic phrasing:  
- Enterprise digital strategy for mission-driven organizations  
- Editorial governance and scalable publishing systems  
- Cross-channel communications leadership  
- Public-sector and advocacy content strategy  
- Audience-centered campaign and content planning
- Consider swapping “messaging” for “content strategy” or “communications strategy” to sound more senior and operationally grounded.
- Keep terms parallel and outcome-oriented; avoid broad labels like “audience-focused” when “audience-centered campaign and content planning” is more specific.
- If space allows, add one differentiator such as “enterprise web modernization” or “AI-enabled content experiences” to reflect recent work.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Enterprise digital strategy” and “editorial systems and governance” duplicate the header and Core Competencies almost verbatim.
- “Multi-channel communications leadership” is already well evidenced in recent NACo and consulting experience.

items.title: Web Platforms & Technical Execution
items.content:
- Drupal
- WordPress
- SharePoint
- Power Pages
- CMS modernization
- HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery
- API integrations
- Workflow automation
- Airtable systems
- AI-enabled search experiences
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong category, but it reads like a raw tool dump and overlaps heavily with the “Technical + IT” section. In Topline Skills, this should emphasize higher-value platform leadership and recent execution themes, not repeat every tool.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from tools to capability clusters: “Drupal & enterprise CMS modernization • Front-end implementation (HTML, CSS, JavaScript) • API integrations & workflow automation • SharePoint and Power Pages • Airtable-based systems • AI-enabled search experiences”
- Drop lower-signal or dated items here, especially “jQuery,” unless it is central to target roles.
- Put the strongest, most recent differentiators first: Drupal, CMS modernization, AI-enabled search, integrations/automation.
- If space allows, make one item outcome-oriented: “Enterprise CMS modernization for high-volume public-sector sites” rather than just “CMS modernization.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This section duplicates the detailed “Technical + IT” lists; keep Topline Skills broader and more strategic.
- “AI-enabled search experiences” already appears in Core Competencies, so avoid overusing the exact phrase elsewhere.

items.title: Analytics, Insights & Optimization
items.content:
- GA4
- Microsoft Clarity
- Looker Studio
- Power BI
- BigQuery
- KPI design
- Leadership reporting
- SEO and performance analysis
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant skill cluster, but it overlaps heavily with “Core Competencies” and “Technical + IT.” Tighten it to emphasize decision-making impact and avoid reading like a duplicate tool list.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from tools-only to capability + outcome: “Analytics infrastructure & insight generation” or “Analytics, Reporting & Optimization.”
- Use grouped phrasing for concision: “GA4, BigQuery, Looker Studio, Power BI and Microsoft Clarity”
- Replace generic items with stronger business-facing language: “KPI framework development,” “executive/leadership dashboards,” “SEO and conversion/performance analysis”
- Suggested rewrite: “GA4, BigQuery, Looker Studio, Power BI and Microsoft Clarity • KPI framework development • Executive dashboarding and leadership reporting • SEO, user behavior and performance analysis”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This largely duplicates “Data, Analytics & Optimization” in Technical + IT; keep Topline Skills more strategic and save full tool inventory for Technical + IT.
- “Analytics and reporting infrastructure” already appears in Core Competencies, so avoid repeating that exact phrasing.

items.title: Multimedia Production & Event Delivery
items.content:
- Video production and editing
- Livestreaming
- PTZ camera systems
- Studio operations
- Hybrid and virtual event production
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This skill block is relevant, but it reads generic and overlaps with both Core Competencies and older NACo bullets. Make it more senior and outcomes-oriented, emphasizing operational ownership rather than basic production tasks.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe for leadership scope: “Broadcast-quality video production • Livestream and hybrid event operations • In-house studio buildout and management • PTZ/multi-camera production systems • Virtual event delivery”
- Replace “video production and editing” with a more senior phrase like “broadcast-quality video production” or “video strategy, production and post-production.”
- Consider swapping “PTZ camera systems” for “multi-camera/PTZ production systems” to sound less equipment-list-like.
- If space allows, tie to impact: “Built and operated in-house studio capacity for advocacy programming, livestreams and recurring multimedia content.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This section overlaps with “Multimedia production and livestream operations” in Core Competencies; use sharper, more specific wording here.
- Avoid repeating older-role language about weekly video updates or podcast production unless those are still central to your current positioning.

items.title: University of Virginia
items.subtitle: Bachelor of Arts (BA), Economics & History
items.content: Ranked among the top public universities in the United States
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: The current line adds little value and reads like generic school marketing. For an experienced candidate, this education entry should be minimal and factual unless you have honors or distinctions worth adding.

Suggested edit:
- Replace the content line entirely with no body text; the degree, school, location, and dates are sufficient.
- If applicable, swap in a concrete credential instead: “Relevant coursework: …” or “Honors: …” only if genuinely strong and still relevant.
- Tighten the subtitle to “B.A., Economics and History” for cleaner formatting.
- Consider dropping dates if you want to reduce age signaling and keep focus on recent senior experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Ranked among the top public universities…” is generic and not candidate-specific, so it weakens the entry rather than strengthening it.
- Avoid adding coursework unless it clearly supports current digital strategy/communications work; otherwise it will feel disconnected from the stronger recent experience.

items.title: Web Platforms & CMS
items.content: Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid platform list, but it’s too bare and overlaps heavily with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution” in Topline Skills. Use this item to signal depth or recency, not just repeat names.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite as: **Drupal (enterprise migrations, modular content architecture) • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages**
- If space allows, prioritize by strength/recency: **Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages**
- Consider adding version/scope only where meaningful, e.g. **Drupal 10** if that aligns with recent project work.
- Keep this item platform-focused; leave implementation details like APIs, HTML/CSS/JS, and automation to adjacent technical sections.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This largely duplicates **Topline Skills > Web Platforms & Technical Execution**; consider removing one list or differentiating this one with proficiency/context.
- GitHub Pages may read as lightweight compared with the rest; keep it only if it supports a visible project or portfolio use case.

items.title: Coding & Technical Implementation
items.content: HTML5 • CSS3 • JavaScript • jQuery • API integrations • Google Tag Manager • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid technical coverage, but this reads as a generic keyword list and overlaps heavily with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution” in Topline Skills. Tighten it to emphasize implementation tools actually used in recent roles and group items more clearly.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite as: “Front-end implementation: HTML5, CSS3, JavaScript, jQuery • Integrations & tagging: APIs, Google Tag Manager • Deployment & automation: GitHub Actions, Cloudflare Workers”
- Use consistent category-led phrasing instead of a flat list; it scans faster and sounds more senior.
- If accurate, replace older terms with stronger/current signals (e.g., “JavaScript” over “jQuery-first”) or add scope like “custom front-end fixes” / “light serverless scripting.”
- Only keep tools you can support with recent examples from freelance/NACo work; otherwise move niche items to projects.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Duplicates “HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery” and “API integrations” already listed under Topline Skills.
- “Google Tag Manager” may fit better under “Data, Analytics & Optimization” unless tagging implementation is a core selling point.

items.title: Automation & Workflow Systems
items.content: Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira • Asana • Basecamp • Slack • Teams • Trello
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid tool coverage, but this reads as a generic software list rather than evidence of workflow automation capability. It also overlaps with “Workflow automation and platform integration” in Core Competencies and “Airtable systems / Workflow automation” in Topline Skills.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe to emphasize systems-building, not just apps: “Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira • Asana • Trello • Slack • Microsoft Teams”
- Remove Basecamp unless it was used recently or materially; it weakens recency and focus.
- Consider renaming the category to “Workflow Automation & Collaboration Systems” for clearer alignment with your recent consulting and NACo work.
- If space allows elsewhere, convert this from a pure list into outcome-linked phrasing, e.g. “Built workflow systems in Airtable, Power Automate and Zapier; managed cross-team delivery in Jira, Asana and Trello.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Slack” and “Teams” are common collaboration tools; keep only if they were central to workflow design, not just everyday communication.
- This item duplicates themes already covered in Core Competencies and Topline Skills; keep the list tighter and more technical.

items.title: Email & Engagement Systems
items.content: Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid, relevant tools, but this item is too bare compared with the rest of the CV and misses the scale/ownership shown in recent NACo roles. It should signal enterprise email operations, not just list platforms.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: **Email Marketing & Engagement Platforms**
- Rewrite as: **Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp — enterprise email and audience engagement platforms used to support newsletter operations, campaign communications and member/stakeholder outreach**
- If accurate, strengthen with scope: **…supporting high-volume newsletters reaching tens of thousands of recipients**
- Keep platform names only if space is tight; otherwise add one functional qualifier such as **segmentation, journeys, list management, campaign deployment**

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This overlaps with work-experience bullets about newsletters and digital channels; avoid repeating audience scale here unless it adds platform-specific context.
- “Multi-channel communications operations” already appears in Core Competencies, so keep this item tool-focused rather than strategic.

items.title: Data, Analytics & Optimization
items.content: GA4 • Microsoft Clarity • Looker Studio • Power BI • BigQuery • SEO • A/B testing • Dashboarding
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant tool stack, but this item overlaps heavily with “Topline Skills > Analytics, Insights & Optimization” and reads as a keyword list rather than a differentiated technical category. Tighten it and emphasize methods/tools not already covered elsewhere.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: Data & Optimization Tools
- Replace with: GA4 • Microsoft Clarity • BigQuery • Looker Studio • Power BI • Google Search Console • A/B testing • KPI reporting
- Swap “SEO” for “Google Search Console” or “performance analysis” to keep this tools-focused and more specific.
- Remove “Dashboarding” since Looker Studio/Power BI already imply it; if space allows, use “conversion analysis” or “user behavior analysis” instead.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This largely duplicates “Topline Skills > Analytics, Insights & Optimization”; consider keeping the broader capability there and making this section strictly platform/tool names.
- GA4, Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio, and BigQuery are already reinforced in the 2022–2024 role, so avoid repeating generic terms here.

items.title: Work Eligibility
items.content: Full legal authorization to work in Belgium (Visa D + residence permit / carte de séjour)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Useful for Belgium-based applications, but the phrasing is a bit legalistic and takes more space than needed. This should read as a clear status note, not a headline achievement.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite for brevity and recruiter scanability: “Authorized to work in Belgium (Visa D and residence permit).”
- If accurate, make it stronger and simpler: “Fully authorized to work in Belgium; residence permit in place.”
- Avoid the French term unless the role specifically requires bilingual administrative terminology; “residence permit” is usually enough.
- Consider moving this into the contact/header area for local applications, since eligibility matters more there than in a secondary rail.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- No major duplication, but this item is lower-value than recent experience; keep it very short so it doesn’t compete for attention.
- If location/contact already signals Belgium and applications are local, this may be optional rather than essential.

items.title: Languages
items.content:
**English** (Native)
**French** (A2/Learning)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is clear but too compressed and visually awkward. It should be reformatted for quick scanning and framed honestly so French supports your Belgium-based role without overstating proficiency.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite as a simple line: Languages: English (native) | French (A2, currently improving)
- Use lowercase proficiency style for consistency and cleaner tone: native, A2, conversational/basic if accurate.
- If relevant to target roles, add practical context only if true: French (A2, professional working improvement underway)
- Keep it concise; this section is supporting information, not a selling point versus your recent digital leadership experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- No major duplication, but avoid overdesign/bolding here; the CV already has strong skills sections competing for attention.
- If space is tight, this can stay in the rail and should not be repeated in the header, summary, or cover letter unless language is job-relevant.

items.title: Soft Skills
items.content: Cross-department coordination • Stakeholder communication • Team leadership • Strategic planning • Clear writing and editing • Problem-solving • Adaptability
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This section is too generic and largely repeats strengths already proven in the summary and core competencies. On a senior CV, “soft skills” should either be removed or reframed as leadership traits tied to scope and outcomes.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to “Leadership Strengths” or “Management & Collaboration” to sound more senior and less filler.
- Cut generic items like “Problem-solving” and “Adaptability”; keep only traits that support target roles.
- Tighten to 4–5 items max, e.g.: Cross-functional leadership • Executive stakeholder management • Editorial judgment • Team development • Strategic planning
- If space is tight, remove this section entirely and use the room for quantified achievements in recent roles.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Cross-department coordination” and “Stakeholder communication” duplicate the header summary and Core Competencies.
- “Team leadership” and “Strategic planning” are already demonstrated more credibly in the 2022–2024 Director role.

items.title: References
items.content: References available upon request.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item adds little value and uses space that could better support recent, higher-impact experience. “References available upon request” is assumed by most employers and usually should be removed.

Suggested edit:
- Delete the “References” entry entirely.
- Use the freed space for stronger supporting content instead, such as a brief “Selected Results” rail item with 1–2 metrics from recent roles.
- If references are specifically requested, provide them separately rather than on the CV.
- If you want a replacement rail item, consider “Work Authorization” or “Languages,” which are more useful and already present here.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This section is redundant because reference availability is standard and does not differentiate you.
- Keeping it may weaken the second-page rail by displacing more relevant, recent qualifications.

items.title: Digital Media Manager / Producer
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Advanced through two digital roles, supporting the creation of the organization’s first in-house digital team and strengthening workflows across web, email, social, and multimedia. Contributed to a major website refresh and produced high-impact digital content—including livestreams and weekly video updates—while providing day-to-day guidance to a digital media associate.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression signal, but the item is still broad and reads as setup rather than impact. Since this is an older role, keep it concise and emphasize foundational contributions that support later leadership roles.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite to foreground progression and team-building: “Promoted across two digital roles to help build NACo’s first in-house digital communications team…”
- Tighten scope and use parallel phrasing: “improved workflows across web, email, social and multimedia; supported a major website refresh; produced livestream and recurring video content.”
- Replace “high-impact” with specifics if available: add output/frequency, audience size, event scale, or engagement gains.
- Clarify supervision modestly: “provided day-to-day direction to a digital media associate” or “helped supervise…” if not a formal manager.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “weekly video updates” overlaps with the next role’s “weekly advocacy video update”; distinguish this as launching/building the format here.
- “strengthening workflows” repeats language used in later NACo roles; frame this as early process-building instead.

items.title: County Solutions & Innovations Coordinator
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Coordinated innovation and research projects supporting organizational programs and policy work. Contributed to digital content production and multimedia materials, and launched the organization’s first podcast, overseeing planning, scripting, and production.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid early-career entry that shows initiative, especially the first podcast launch. It should be tightened and framed around outcomes/ownership, while keeping multimedia language distinct from later NACo roles.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite to emphasize scope and initiative: “Coordinated innovation and research initiatives supporting NACo programs and policy priorities.”
- Make the podcast achievement the lead proof point: “Launched NACo’s first podcast, leading concept development, scripting, guest coordination and production.”
- Trim generic phrasing like “contributed to digital content production and multimedia materials”; replace with a clearer contribution such as “produced digital and multimedia content to support program communications.”
- If possible, add one measurable detail: number of episodes, audience, internal stakeholders supported, or types of projects delivered.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Digital content production and multimedia” overlaps with later digital/media roles; keep this entry focused on research/program support plus the podcast launch.
- Avoid overstating team leadership here, since stronger management progression appears in later NACo positions.

items.title: Multimedia & Creative Tools
items.content: Premiere Pro • Audition • Photoshop • Illustrator • Livestream studio workflows • Podcast production
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is relevant, but it overlaps heavily with “Multimedia production and livestream operations” in Core Competencies and “Multimedia Production & Event Delivery” in Topline Skills. Make it more tool-specific and concise, with production capabilities framed in stronger, current language.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: Multimedia Tools
